description: Generated from phase package manifests, detected audio assets, and benchmark-authored audio provenance.

audio.strategy: One synthesized piano-like voice computed in pure TypeScript DSP at 44.1 kHz (fundamental plus a slightly inharmonic decaying partial stack with an ADSR-style envelope, velocity-dependent gain and brightness). No recorded samples, no network, no device required. The browser drains the engine into the speakers via the Web Audio path; tests render PCM directly for deterministic verification.

notes: Phase 1 provides exactly one dependable basic piano voice; the phase spec explicitly permits 'honestly-described synthesis'. This synthesized voice is never described as a recording.
The sustain pedal, keyboard mute/blur cleanup, MIDI disconnect cleanup, and unmount cleanup all silence every owned voice (all-notes-off).
Every panel control from the visual spec is present, moves/presses accessibly, and changes presentation state only; no panel control claims to alter audio or system state in Phase 1.

audio.strategy: One Web Audio AudioContext realizes the browser signal path: per-layer bus GainNodes (Piano A, Piano B) drain a single deterministic pure-DSP StageEngine, then feed an ordered per-layer effect chain (Mod 1, Mod 2, Delay, Amp Sim/EQ, Compressor, Reverb, shared Rotary when routed) and a shared master GainNode (Master Level) + DynamicsCompressor limiter into one destination. The effects are real DSP operating on PCM, so tests render stereo blocks and measure that every unit/type/bypass/routing changes the audio; the browser context is injectable so graph tests verify one context, one destination, and full cleanup without a device. Grand, Upright, and Electric are bundled, offline, redistributable multi-root/multi-velocity sample libraries generated deterministically (many root notes across E1..E7 plus three velocity layers, so uniform pitch-shifting of a single note is not audible) and rendered as committed WAV assets under public/samples; Clav, Digital, and Misc are honest live synthesis (per the piano spec sourceRules). Generated sample tables are truthfully declared as generated, never as field recordings.

audio.strategy: One Web Audio AudioContext realizes the browser signal path. The Phase 3 instrument is a single System4 pure-DSP engine that mixes the Piano (2 layers), Organ (2 layers sharing one effect chain) and Synth (3 layers with independent effect chains) into ONE shared Rotary and ONE master GainNode (Master Level) + DynamicsCompressor limiter feeding exactly one destination, realized by one SystemGraph drain node — no second AudioContext, nothing bypasses the master path. Each effect chain keeps the documented order (Mod 1, Mod 2, Delay, Amp Sim/EQ, Compressor, Reverb, then Rotary when routed). The engine is deterministic and sample-accurate, so tests render real PCM and prove every engine/model/drawbar/wave/filter/envelope/morph/split/scene changes the audio; the browser context is injectable so graph tests verify one context, one destination, and full cleanup. Grand, Upright, and Electric remain bundled, offline, redistributable multi-root/multi-velocity sample libraries generated deterministically (many root notes across E1..E7 plus three velocity layers) and rendered as committed WAV assets under public/samples; Clav, Digital, and Misc are honest live synthesis (piano spec sourceRules); the Organ and Synth engines are honest live additive/oscillator synthesis. Generated sample tables and DSP are truthfully declared as generated, never as field recordings.

notes: One Web Audio AudioContext (browser path) or injected context (tests) realizes the full System4 drain, the ordered effect chains (shared Rotary last), Master Level, the limiter, and one destination; dispose() disconnects every node and closes the context (cleanup). The pure-DSP System4 is the audible signal graph and is what cross-boundary tests render.
Grand, Upright, and Electric are bundled, offline, redistributable sample sets (multi-root, multi-velocity) declared truthfully as generated sample tables, not field recordings.

The Organ and Synth engines are honest live synthesis (additive/oscillator DSP); model/wave/filter/envelope/morph distinctions are real and proven by rendered-PCM tests, never described as recordings.

Programs round-trip all supported state (piano/organ/synth/effects/splits/scenes/morphs/clock/transpose) across 32 slots + 8 Live; Store/Store As/dirty/edit-discard and Live auto-store are implemented. Master Level is excluded from program state (spec).

Splits (up to 4 zones, 3 points, Off/+/-6/+/-12 crossfades), Layer Scenes I/II, Wheel and Control Pedal morphs (assignment, interpolation, indicators, clearing), Master Clock (tap + dial), Transpose +/-6 and Shift+Transpose Panic behave canonically.

Unsupported (spec-excluded, listed as such): preset library, banks beyond one, Extern/Aux KB and all menus, aftertouch morph (A.T. button decorative), arpeggiator pattern editing/zig-zag/accent/pan, Filter/LFO/Arp Group modes, swell pedal, percussion poly mode.
Sustain honors SUSTPED per enabled layer; String Res and Soft Release remain honest approximations; asset failure enters a labeled playable fallback without reporting ready.
